_meta.held_out: Both requirements name work this repository has open and has not done, so neither arm can be written from a remembered solution.
_meta.not_a_result: This file fixes the requirement, target, evaluator, carrier, base commit, reviewer rubric and budget before either arm runs, and contains no outcome field of any kind. It is validated by `python3 scripts/measure_delivery_shape.py plan <this file>`, which refuses any measured field appearing here. Executing the pair produces a separate delivery-shape-experiment/v1 record; this file is never edited to match what happened.
_meta.provenance: Pre-registered from open issue #322; the tree it plans does not exist yet.

planned_units.purpose: Deliver the whole requirement as one review unit.

A.requirement_text:
Migrate two already-shipped Skill refactors onto the proof-carrying protocol.

Introduce one proof-record schema plus a deterministic checker with a planted-defect selftest, express the repo-agent-native v2 refactor and the shared-skills-infra index-guard refactor as records against that schema, and register the protocol in an architecture note. A record names the golden proof it preserves; a refactor with no preserved proof is refused rather than recorded. No existing checker may be relaxed to admit a record.
A.reviewer_rubric:
Advisory reviewer rubric, identical for both arms and non-binding by construction:
1. Can a reviewer state, per review unit, what would have to be true for the unit to be wrong?
2. Is every claim in the unit's description anchored to a file the unit actually changes?
3. Does the unit leave a cheap way to make it go red?
4. Is anything in the unit unrelated to the requirement text?
A reviewer score never overturns a deterministic failure; it is recorded as reviewer_findings and read alongside, not instead of, the gate result.

planned_units.purpose: Schema and checker every later unit is written against.
First consumer: the v2 refactor stated as a proof record.
Path-disjoint sibling of B2: the index-guard refactor.
Registers the protocol only once both records exist.
